voyage.name: Historic Half-timbered Houses
voyage.content: Unlike the city center, Bornheim largely survived the war intact, preserving its charming medieval and baroque half-timbered houses. Strolling along the Berger Straße offers an authentic glimpse into the former village structure of Bornheim.

voyage.name: Goetheturm
voyage.content: An old 43-metre wooden tower with viewing platform offering nice views of the skyline. It burned down in 2017, but has since been rebuilt.

voyage.name: Frankfurter Zoo
voyage.content: Established in 1858, this is one of the oldest zoos in the world. It gained international fame under the direction of Bernhard Grzimek, who pioneered animal conservation. The zoo focuses on modern enclosure design and houses a wide array of species in the heart of the city.

voyage.name: Höchst Old Town
voyage.content: A remarkably preserved medieval area with half-timbered houses and narrow streets. Key highlights include the 9th-century St. Justin's Church (Frankfurt's oldest building), the castle, and the baroque Bolongaro Palace with its gardens. Porcelain enthusiasts should visit the Porcelain Museum in the Kronberger House and the nearby manufacturing center.

voyage.name: Frankfurt Airport Tours
voyage.hours: Daily by appointment; check website for tour slots
voyage.content: As one of Europe's busiest hubs, the airport offers behind-the-scenes insights. Guided tours provide access to the airfield and specialized areas, such as the impressive fire department facilities. Advance booking online is mandatory.

voyage.name: The Dresden Frankfurt Dance Company
voyage.content: Modern ballet in Frankfurt playing at the Bockenheimer Depot.

voyage.name: River cruises along the Main River
voyage.content: There are two companies offering river cruises along the Main River, and both of them depart from Mainkai near the Eiserner Steg bridge in the Old Town. There are short sightseeing cruises as well as longer tours heading towards the Rhein river and its scenic spots.

voyage.name: Goethe Institut
voyage.content: The official German language institute with a vast range of courses to learn German in Goethe's hometown.

voyage.name: Johann Wolfgang Goethe University
voyage.content: Founded in 1914, this urban university offers a wide range of faculties. Today, the university has 38,000 students on 4 major campuses: Campus Bockenheim, Campus Riedberg, Campus Westend, Campus Niederrad.

voyage.name: Volkshochschule Frankfurt
voyage.content: Vast range of language courses, cooking classes and other educational courses.

voyage.name: Hessen Shop
voyage.content: Small chain of shops selling unique locally produced or locally themed goods. Locations in Bockenheim (Leipziger Straße 49), Sachsenhausen (Diesterwegstraße 22), and downtown in Kleinmarkthalle (Hasengasse 5).

voyage.name: Best Worscht in Town
voyage.content: Place where you can try "Curry-Wurst", which is a sliced beef sausage served with ketchup and curry spices, and considered one of the most popular German fast food products. The Best Worscht in Town chain is special in that it also serves extremely spicy variants, using some of the hottest spices available from different parts of the world. There have even been televised hot sausage eating competitions with on-site m

voyage.name: Römerberg
voyage.content: Römerberg is the historic centre of Frankfurt, with a number of beautiful buildings, including the town hall and a church from the 14th and 15th century. The name Römer itself refers to the town hall of Frankfurt, which itself received this name from the prominent main building , which has existed since at least 1322 and was bought by the city administration in 1405. Fortunately, large parts of the Römer's façade sur

voyage.name: Dom-Römer-Areal
voyage.content: Urban revitalization of the Dom-Römer complex, in which a number of old historic buildings have been rebuilt from scratch – incorporating only a few original artifacts – based on old pictures and drawings. The area includes the Steinerne Haus at Markt 44, a medieval-looking building first erected in 1464 that had already been rebuilt in the 1960s. The street known as Alter Markt or simply as Markt was in fact one of

voyage.name: Kaiserdom
voyage.alt: Frankfurt Cathedral/Imperial Cathedral of Saint Bartholomew
voyage.content: The main cathedral with its 95 m high tower, built in Gothic style in the 14th century. From 1562 to 1792, emperors of the Holy Roman Empire were crowned in the cathedral. It is possible to ascend the tower to a platform at 66 m height, affording excellent views over the city. For this, you will need to enter via a separate entrance at the southern side of the cathedral and climb over 300 steps in a narrow winding st

voyage.name: Eiserner Steg
voyage.content: Relatively well-known bridge for pedestrians, built in 1869. It is just a minute away from the Römer. Crossing the bridge leads you to Sachsenhausen and provides good views of the skyline.

voyage.name: Paulskirche
voyage.content: A church with important political symbolism in Germany. This was the seat of the first democratically elected parliament in Germany in 1848. Here the revolutionaries wrote the 1848 constitution that sadly was never put into effect. Like most historic buildings in the city centre, it was destroyed during World War II, but was also among the first buildings to be rebuilt after 1945 (with different interior). Today the

voyage.name: Liebfrauenkirche
voyage.content: 14th century Roman Catholic church and monastery.

voyage.name: St. Leonhardskirche
voyage.content: Late Romanic church built in 1219, and transformed in accordance with the Gothic style in the 15th century. English-language Catholic mass service on Saturdays and Sundays.

voyage.name: Staufenmauer
voyage.content: Remains of the old city wall (1138–1254) can be seen in the Fahrgasse and at the Liebfrauenkirche. More prominent examples of the city fortification built in later years include the Eschenheimer Turm (1428) near Hauptwache and the Friedberger Warte (1478, rebuilt 1637), which is on the Friedberger Landstraße a bit outside the main city centre.

voyage.name: Kunsthalle Schirn
voyage.price: Ticket prices vary depending on the exhibitions
voyage.content: A museum specializing in contemporary art. It is located just off the Römerplatz. There are two exhibition spaces that rotate every month or two.

voyage.name: Museum für Moderne Kunst
voyage.content: The building was designed by Hans Hollein to resemble a boat, which is most notable when approaching it from the back (east). Apart from well-known artists in the permanent collection, e.g. Roy Liechtenstein and Andy Warhol, the museum has changing exhibits that often include contemporary works. The museum has an associated restaurant Triangolo.

voyage.name: Frankfurter Kunstverein
voyage.content: Constantly changing contemporary art expositions.

voyage.name: Archäologisches Museum
voyage.price: Adults €7, reduced €3.50, under 18 years free, free entry every last Saturday of the month
voyage.content: In a building which used to house a Carmelite monastery.

voyage.name: Historisches Museum
voyage.content: Historic museum of the city of Frankfurt and its citizens. Today it offers a wide collection of the history of the city.

voyage.name: Caricatura Museum for Comic Art
voyage.content: Museum for comic art, i.e., satire and illustrations. Located in the old Leinwandhaus (Linen House), a historic building that was first constructed in 1396–1399, but only reopened in 1984 after suffering substantial damage in World War II.

voyage.name: Kleinmarkthalle
voyage.hours: Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00, Sat 08:00-16:00, Sun and holidays closed
voyage.content: A market hall with a large variety of local and international vendors ranging from fresh produce to ready-to-eat food and drinks.

voyage.name: Farmer's Market at Konstablerwache
voyage.content: Locally produced vegetables or fruits are found also directly from regional ecological producers.

voyage.name: Zum Alten Frankfurter
voyage.content: It feels like a family run place. Intimate and quiet. Food freshly cooked with passion. Schnitzel: the breading throws bubbles the way it should be. The service charming and quick. All in all a nice experience.

voyage.name: China Garten
voyage.content: If you want to eat quality and tasty Asian food and that at great prices, you have to go here. The service is always very friendly.

voyage.name: Tonbul Grill und Kebap Haus
voyage.content: Delicious "homemade" doner kebab with a unique touch. Not a standard kebab. Super nice place with homemade fresh products. The sauces are very yummy. The staff is also very friendly.

voyage.name: Paulaner am Dom
voyage.content: Traditional Bavarian restaurant, perhaps a bit touristy, right behind the cathedral near Römer. It's difficult to get a table at weekends without a reservation.

voyage.name: Salzkammer
voyage.content: The restaurant serves food close to real Austrian cuisine.

voyage.name: Die Rote Bar
voyage.content: This cocktail bar offers excellent drinks in a stylish atmosphere. The bar has its own whiskey selection. Better be well dressed for the door. Coming late, one has to wait a bit outside until space is found inside.

voyage.name: Cafe & Bar Celona
voyage.content: Daily 09:00-01:00, F Sa 09:00-02:00. Spanish-style bar in the heart of the city. Popular, attracts a younger crowd, good for meeting people. Very crowded around 17:00-19:00. Also serves a variety of Spanish dishes. €7-20/person.

voyage.name: Wacker´s Kaffee Geschäft
voyage.content: Since 1914 known for its good coffee. Very packed over lunch time but has its own roast of coffee. Don't mind a long queue, the crew is dedicated and you will never wait more than five minutes for your coffee

voyage.name: Hauptwache
voyage.content: A public area that is often considered the central hub of Frankfurt's modern downtown area due to its importance as a public transportation station and its central location, right between the main shopping street (Zeil) and the Rossmarkt (another public square), and just south of the 15th-century Eschenheimer Turm (Eschenheim Tower). The place is named after a Baroque building ("Hauptwache") more or less in its centr

voyage.name: Alte Oper
voyage.content: Renaissance Opera Building in the centre of the city. A busy square with fountains can be found in front of it. It was opened in 1880, but it has not been used for operas since the rebuilding after the war, but for concerts, congresses, and similar "fancy" events.

voyage.name: Börse Frankfurt
voyage.content: The Frankfurt stock exchange building, still in use, see the bull and bear statues just outside. You cannot enter the building unless you have registered for a guided tour at least one working day in advance.

voyage.name: Palmengarten
voyage.content: The Palmengarten is one of two botanical gardens in Frankfurt. There are special exhibitions and events throughout the much of the year.

voyage.name: Botanischer Garten
voyage.hours: Mar-Oct: Mon-Sat 09:00-18:00, Sun and holidays 09:00-13:00; Nov-Feb: closed

voyage.name: Grüneburgpark
voyage.content: This is Frankfurt's largest public park. Even though there are many parks in Frankfurt, the Grüneburgpark is probably the most liked. It is close to two campuses of the university: many young people meet there, and many business people jog there after work.

voyage.name: Campus Westend
voyage.content: Architecturally interesting campus of the Johann Wolfgang Goethe-University. Includes the IG Farben building, the former corporate headquarters of IG Farben and largest office building in Europe from 1930 until the 1950s.

voyage.name: Palais Thurn und Taxis
voyage.content: 18th-century palace of the Princely House of Thurn and Taxis. In the 19th century, it served as the parliament of the German Confederation. Unfortunately, apart from the front façade, most of it is reconstructed. The reconstruction has a smaller scale than the building's original 18th-century size.

voyage.name: Hauptfriedhof
voyage.content: Main cemetery, where you can find several mausoleums, over 150 year old tombstones, and the final resting places of philosophers Arthur Schopenhauer and Theodor W. Adorno.

voyage.name: Katharinenkirche
voyage.content: Baroque-style Lutheran church at Hauptwache. Constructed 1678 to 1681 at the site of a former monastery, destroyed during World War II, and restored 1950 to 1954. The tower stands 54 m tall.

voyage.name: Literaturhaus Frankfurt
voyage.content: Former public library building, constructed 1820-1825 in neo-classical style.

voyage.name: Amtsgericht und Landgericht Frankfurt
voyage.content: Frankfurt's courts are housed in an ensemble of buildings, including the main building erected in 1884–1889 in Neo-Renaissance style and a second building just behind it built in 1913–17 in Neoclassic style.

voyage.name: Odeon
voyage.content: Small museum building built in 1816, now housing a dance club.

voyage.name: Stiftstraße 6-10
voyage.content: Beautiful historic buildings built in 1903. Stiftstraße 8–10 is a rare example of Art nouveau in Frankfurt. Stiftstraße 6 has a colorful façade.

voyage.name: Main Tower
voyage.content: This building is special as it is the only Frankfurt high-rise tower that is open to the public with an elevator to the viewing platform at a height of 200 m. From here, you will have a good view of Frankfurt and the surrounding area. Make sure to go on a clear day, and if you're in Frankfurt in Autumn or Spring you might wish to try to go up a short while before sunset. That way, you can witness how the city changes

voyage.name: Jüdisches Museum
voyage.price: Admission with audio guide: €7, children €3.50, including Museum Judengasse: €10
voyage.content: The Jewish community in Frankfurt can look back on over 850 years of history in the city and is the second oldest Jewish community in Germany. The well funded museum in the old Rothschild (they originate from Frankfurt) palace pays tribute to this history with a strong focus on the holocaust.

voyage.name: Museum Judengasse
voyage.price: Adults €6, reduced €3, free every last Saturday of the month
voyage.content: It is part of the Jewish Museum, but at a different address (not anywhere near the Museumsufer). It reopened after refurbishment in 2016. Here are exhibited the foundations from the Jewish Ghetto dating back to 1462, as well as information about life as a Jewish person in this ghetto during the Middle Ages. Info is in English & German. Outside of this museum is the "Holocaust Memorial Wall" with over 11,000 names of

voyage.name: Goethe-Haus und -Museum
voyage.content: Birthplace of Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, Germany's most famous author and poet. It's a museum and picture gallery devoted to Goethe.

voyage.name: Naturmuseum Senckenberg
voyage.content: Commonly called just Senckenberg museum it is one of the most famous museums in Frankfurt. The Senckenberg has various exhibits on natural history; plants, animals, minerals, and so on; the biggest attraction are the dinosaur skeletons and the collection of preserved animals that were hunted and stuffed in a less enlightened age. Highly recommended for anybody interested in the subject. Also suitable for children, wh

voyage.name: Geldmuseum der Deutschen Bundesbank
voyage.alt: Money Museum of the German Central Bank
voyage.content: A museum about money and its history.

voyage.name: Experiminta
voyage.content: Interactive science museum focusing on hands-on exhibits.

voyage.name: Anne Frank Educational Center
voyage.hours: Sat Sun 12:00-18:00, Mon-Fri closed (exceptions for groups with appointment)
voyage.content: The well-known young Holocaust victim Anne Frank was born in Frankfurt and first lived with her family in a house at Marbachweg 307, just minutes away from this centre, before they moved to Ganghofer Straße 24, which is a few blocks further north. Based on her biography, the Anne Frank Educational Center relies on interactive methods to promote tolerance and educate people about the consequences of Nazism, discrimina

voyage.name: Cinestar Metropolis
voyage.content: The cinema shows a couple of movies in English.

voyage.name: English theatre
voyage.content: See a play at the largest English-language theatre in continental Europe

voyage.name: Oper Frankfurt
voyage.content: Not to be confused with the historic Alte Oper building, this modern building is where to go to see an opera performance. State subsidized performances make this a relatively affordable place to see high quality productions

voyage.name: Bockenheimer Depot
voyage.content: A theatre venue of the Städtische Bühnen Frankfurt, for opera and dance performances.

voyage.name: Schillermarkt
voyage.content: Fresh meals and local products are sold at the groceries market directly in the centre at this shopping street.

voyage.name: Skyline Plaza
voyage.content: The shopping centre opened in the summer 2013. It has it own parking. There is a terasse on top with a café. Otherwise you'll find around 170 different shops.

voyage.name: Grüneburger Bioladen
voyage.content: Excellent choice of cheese and fresh vegetables. The shop has affordable lunch soups and also does custom deliveries.

voyage.name: Petersen Gutes Essen
voyage.content: Sells gourmet food. It has bread, cheese, fresh pasta, pasterys and a lot more.

voyage.name: Strahmann Baguetterie & Cafébar
voyage.content: the best focaccias in town! Also they have a huge variety of other sandwiches, salads, snacks etc. Sometimes the queue is long.

voyage.name: Pizzeria 7 Bello
voyage.content: Good lunch option for fast pizza and pasta. Popular during summer as they have a small terrace on the side walk.

voyage.name: Ruchi
voyage.content: A very short walk north from the main train station you find daily Indian all-you-can-eat tasty buffet and at a good value. South Indian buffet on Saturdays. Idly, dosas, vada, pani puri, Manchurian, and bajjis are all available. Very friendly staff.

voyage.name: Fennischfuchser
voyage.content: Try some traditional food here. Rustic ambience. A somewhat dark restaurant inside.

voyage.name: Ristorante Punto e Pasta 1998
voyage.content: A really friendly little pizzeria. Hidden behind the main train station. The pizzas are really tasty, crispy crust, thin dough and aromatic topping. Good traditional Italian service.

voyage.name: Tatie Restaurant
voyage.content: Very good restaurant that offers Moroccan cuisine. The plates are generous and the servers professional. Clean and nicely decorated restaurant.

voyage.name: Im Herzen Afrikas
voyage.content: Eastern African food. Decoration is special (sand as floor) and reservation is important, as for dinner they offer only specific times.

voyage.name: Saravanaa Bhavan
voyage.content: Purely vegetarian, authentic South Indian cuisine.

voyage.name: Bidlabu
voyage.content: Bistro-style bar with special lunch menus and excellent specific dinner food. One can sit in the street and enjoy a good glass of wine, a long drink or a fancy cocktails like "Dark and Stormy". There are many Gins to choose from.

voyage.name: Der Fette Bulle
voyage.content: Hipster burger place near the train station. Good food and nice atmosphere.

voyage.name: Iwase
voyage.content: Considered by many to be the best Japanese food in the city. Not much larger than a hole in the wall, but the staff is authentic Japanese, and the food delicious.

voyage.name: Koh Samui
voyage.content: The Thai restaurant has many choices and offers more than decent green curry for reasonable prices.

voyage.name: Orfeo's Erben
voyage.content: One of the most popular restaurants.

voyage.name: Quan Van
voyage.content: The Vietnamese kitchen is said to be excellent and offers Vietnamese food to affordable prices.

voyage.name: Cantina Divino
voyage.content: Not a big menu, but it changes rapidly the excellent Italian food. The restaurant is very popular and hence crowded. Offers Sicilian wines.

voyage.name: Moriki
voyage.content: The Japanese kitchen with Asian fusion elements mixed in is located in the basement of the Deutsche Bank tower. It does fine prepared Sushis. The mousse au chocolat is recommended. They offer a wide choice of Sake

voyage.name: Main Nizza
voyage.content: Popular business lunch set and Mediterranean food for dinner. There is some vegetarian choice or for pescatarian fresh sea food. They have a nice terrace in summer on the river bank, where one can take just a coffee. The view over the Main is lovely and the interior is well decorated. Not only for the good food the restaurant received the 2013 German "Gastronomie" price.

voyage.name: Alte Kanzlei
voyage.content: Traditional Italian restaurant close by to the Alte Oper and Deutsche Bank in Westend.

voyage.name: Volkswirtschaft
voyage.content: It streams important football matches. The tavern is usually very packed.

voyage.name: Club Voltaire
voyage.content: Since 1962 exists this cultural tavern. It offers drinks for mixed public of all ages. Sometimes it asks for entry for the musicians or lecturers, but generally it is free entry.

voyage.name: Cafehaus Siesmayer
voyage.content: In the middle of a great location of the Grüneburgpark and next to the palm garden serves in Viennese café style pastries.

voyage.name: Hoppenworth & Ploch
voyage.content: The student café is serving and selling excellent espressos. They are proud about their barrista knowledge. The room is not only flooded by the many students of the campus, but by excellent café flavour and electronic music. They are roasting themselves the specific well chosen beans.

voyage.name: Gibson Club
voyage.content: The Gibson club has a chic and urban atmosphere. They have both live and DJ acts. It opened in spring 2012. The long lines outside the nightclub move fast.

voyage.name: Jazzkeller
voyage.content: Since 1952 the Jazz meeting point. Outstanding Jazz music for everyone with special concerts once in a while.

voyage.name: Tanzhaus West
voyage.content: The club is mostly known for drum and bass music. It has a relaxed public. The website has details on the performing artists. During summertime the back is open also on Sundays for relaxing with good music.

voyage.name: Velvet Club
voyage.content: Club in downtown Frankfurt with very nice interior design. Great place for house and electronic music lovers.

voyage.name: Zoom
voyage.content: Jazz, Reggae, Dancehall and Rock club for the middle aged (30-50 yr) with special guests and regular themes. It is the successor of the Sinkkasten artsclub and attracts many indie-bands.

voyage.name: Five Elements Hostel
voyage.content: Clean and new facilities with English and German speaking staff. Offers variation from dorms to single rooms. Free Wi-Fi.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Express Frankfurt City Hauptbahnhof
voyage.content: WiFi and breakfast included in the room price.

voyage.name: ibis Styles Frankfurt City
voyage.content: WiFi and breakfast included in the room price.

voyage.name: Hotel Ambassador
voyage.content: Rooms are okay, proximity to the train station a plus (about 5 minutes on foot). Near the red light district which is a minus (you don't have to actually walk through the red light district to get to the hotel though).

voyage.name: Hotel Concorde
voyage.content: Close to main station with good breakfast. Free WLAN. All rooms with air conditioning. For long-term residents it offers apartments, too.

voyage.name: Corner Hotel
voyage.content: Modern and clean hotel with 50 rooms and rather basic interior.

voyage.name: Manhattan Hotel
voyage.content: Small and clean hotel opposite main station, so perfect for early departures and/or late arrivals. Free WLAN and good buffet breakfast with multilingual staff. Rooms are good but avoid rooms facing the street as the area is busy late at night

voyage.name: Novotel Frankfurt City
voyage.content: More than 235 rooms in a solid business traveller hotel. Next to the trade fair ground and has loads of conference rooms.

voyage.name: Topas Hotel
voyage.content: Owner-operated hotel in a side street of main station. Renovated, friendly service but just 33 clean rooms. Free newspaper

voyage.name: Frankfurt Marriott Hotel
voyage.content: A typical early 1990s Marriott in a highrise tower, complete with a Champions bar. Splendid views from upper floors as most other towers are some distance away.

voyage.name: MGallery Hotel Savigny Fankfurt
voyage.content: The former Sofitel started to age badly and rather than update it, Accor downgraded it to an MGallery. A taste of erstwhile luxury can be had at really reasonable rates outside of trade fair dates. You will, however, have to contend with worn furniture and fixtures and partially indifferent staff. The Savigny is at the border of a quiet residential lowrise district and the highrise quarter, so you can enjoy the best

voyage.name: NH Frankfurt Messe
voyage.content: The other NH in Frankfurt is a more contemporary affair, with rooms featuring fresh green accents in line with NH's latest interior design guidelines.

voyage.name: Radisson BLU Hotel
voyage.content: The hotel is an eye-catcher because it looks like a blue coin on the edge. It is just located at the border of Rödelheim and Bockenheim.

voyage.name: Frankfurter Hof
voyage.content: The grand old hotel of Frankfurt and known for excellent style and service for more than 130 years.

voyage.name: Intercontinental Frankfurt
voyage.content: Major business hotel and conference centre for international travelers. Also home to loads of conventions. Amazing view from club rooms over the city.

voyage.name: The Pure
voyage.content: Puristic but excellent Design Hotel north side of central station. A must stay for every style fan with fancy lounge, great cocktails & attentive staff.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu hotel
voyage.content: This architecturally outstanding hotel (the building is actually is the shape of a wheel standing on its side) is very popular with business travellers. Free W-Lan for guests and good location to trade fair.

voyage.name: Westin Grand Frankfurt
voyage.content: Fresh city centre hotel with calm rooms. Lots of international guests but staff with good local knowledge.

voyage.name: 25 hours Frankfurt by Levi's
voyage.content: This hotel by the German "lifestyle hotel" chain features design elements inspired by the Levi's jeans brand. The rooms are in different colours 1960s or 70s or 80s style. There is a music rehearsal room on location as well, available for rent.

voyage.name: Le Meridien Parkhotel
voyage.content: In a quiet square immediately south of the Hauptbahnhof, this hotel blends a historic 19th century building and a more modern 20th century one, and such a blend is to be found in the hotel's interior design too, done with the typical German charm. Despite charging arm and leg for almost all services, including WiFi, the hotel often finds its 300 rooms fully booked.

voyage.name: Jumeirah Frankfurt
voyage.content: The Jumeirah occupies a lean sky-high tower rising out of the MyZeil shopping centre, right behind the Thurn und Taxis palace. Elegant decor with extensive use of dark hardwood panelling.

voyage.name: European Central Bank
voyage.content: This skyscaper complex is the seat of European financial power and decisions. The building was completed in 2014. Guided tours are available but advance registration is required.

voyage.name: Bornheim
voyage.content: A nice residential quarter with a lively market and beautiful medieval houses which survived the war intact (unlike the city centre). The most important and lively street is the Berger Straße, which runs from downtown all the way to the oldest parts of Bornheim. The more central downtown part of the Berger Straße (actually in the Nordend district) features a variety of small and often trendy little stores, cafés, and

voyage.name: Dialogmuseum
voyage.content: Experience the world as blind people do. Guided tour through rooms in complete darkness, led by blind or visually impaired staff members. In each room, you experience a different daily life situation (e.g., walking through a park, a boat trip, visiting a bar).

voyage.name: Lohrberg
voyage.content: Head up the Lohrberg, where you can enjoy beautiful views of the city, as well as of the local vineyard (the last remaining one in Frankfurt). There is a small restaurant with outdoor seating and an apple orchard serving homemade apple juice and Ebbelwoi (local cider). Other amenities include a small pool for children and a barbecue area (bring your own).

voyage.name: Ice skating ring
voyage.content: Ice skating for amateurs or watch ice hockey games by the local teams.

voyage.name: Boulderwelt Frankfurt
voyage.content: Opened in the winter of 2012, this hall is still expanding and has boulders in various difficulties for beginners to experienced ones. The route setter is very experienced and the crew friendly. Only the air can get "powdry" at peak times. From time to time there are organised competitions.

voyage.name: Kletterzentrum Frankfurt/Main
voyage.content: The DAV Kletterzentrum opened for climbing in spring 2013. It offers up to 15 m high walls with many routes.

voyage.name: Dynochrom
voyage.content: This gym has tough boulders for enthusiastic climbers.

voyage.name: Pizzeria Charly Braun
voyage.content: A small place with cheap and excellent pizza. Pasta and salad also served. Locals usually call in an order and pick up in twenty minutes.

voyage.name: Sandbar
voyage.content: This place has small snacks and good wines.

voyage.name: Batschkapp
voyage.content: The place for rock and alternative music. One of the oldest clubs in town (since 1976). The club moved enthusiastically to the new place in 2013.

voyage.name: Robert Johnson
voyage.content: They don't announce who is playing for that one has to subscribe to the monthly newsletter to know. It is usual playing minimal electronic music. The club has a terrace and beautiful view over the main. The sound system is refined and the décor minimalistic. The door is usually not that selective, but better have female presence in the group.

voyage.name: Frankfurt Airport's Airport Tours
voyage.content: Frankfurt Airport, one of the busiest in Europe, offers several different guided tours, including a Fire Department Tour.

voyage.name: Henninger Turm
voyage.content: A 120 m tall tower. Inaugurated in 1961, it remained by far the highest grain storage silo tower in the world until 2005. The top part used to have rotating restaurants and observation decks. The silo tower was demolished in 2013, and rebuilt as a modern residential tower with a similar external appearance. A new restaurant is slated to open at the top.

voyage.name: Hindemith Cabinet in the Cowherds' Tower
voyage.hours: Sun 11:00-18:00, Mon-Sat closed (exceptions for groups with appointment)
voyage.content: The Cowherds' Tower is a 14th century tower and city gate. The German composer Paul Hindemith lived in this tower between 1923 and 1927. Today it contains a small museum about the composer, and a music room for chamber concerts and other events.

voyage.name: Portikus
voyage.hours: Tue-Fri 12:00-18:00, Sat Sun 11:00-19:00, also closed when there is no current exhibition and on some public holidays
voyage.content: An institution exhibiting contemporary art of emerging and established artists. It was founded in 1987 and is part of the Städelschule (Staatliche Hochschule für Bildende Künste, a school of art).

voyage.name: Städel-Museum
voyage.price: €12, reduced: €10, Sa-Su & holidays: €14, reduced: €12, Familyticket (2 adults and at least one child): €24, children under 12 free
voyage.content: It is named after Johann Friedrich Staedel. The museum displays various works of art, both modern and old. There are also varying exhibitions at any time. Behind the museum is the Städelschule, an art school with a cheap cafeteria.

voyage.name: Museum Giersch
voyage.alt: Museum of Regional Historic Art and Culture
voyage.content: The broad exhibition range covers all types of art – painting, photography, sculpture, graphic art, architecture and applied arts. Usually the exhibitions focus on artist that have some sort of connection to Frankfurt or the Frankfurt region. It presents works on loan from public and private owners, which are often stored in depots or private collections and therefore not otherwise accessible to the general public. T

voyage.name: Museum für Angewandte Kunst
voyage.content: The museum for applied arts and design hosts just that in a beautiful Richard Meier designed building. The small park around it is a popular hangout in summer and there is a small posh restaurant on the ground floor.

voyage.name: Liebieghaus - Skulpturensammlung
voyage.content: Large collection of sculptures and statues from all over the world. Very nice cafe in the garden.

voyage.name: Museum der Weltkulturen
voyage.content: Due to a lack of space and funding, it doesn't display its permanent ethnographic collection but rather shows well-made exhibitions.

voyage.name: Museum für Kommunikation
voyage.price: €6 for adults; €1.50 for youth 5-17; children until 4 free
voyage.content: Formerly known as the postal museum, it explains the history of communication with a strong focus on postal services and telecommunication. The permanent exhibition shows the developments in communication techniques from telegraphs, to telephones to the internet. A lot of old telegraphs, phones, fax machines etc. are on display. Descriptions in both English and German. The museum has many interactive parts which are

voyage.name: Deutsches Architekturmuseum
voyage.content: The Architecture Museum displays various types of exhibits about buildings and architecture. Their tagline is "From Primordial Hut to Skyscraper". There's also a small cafe in the DAM.

voyage.name: Deutsches Filmmuseum
voyage.hours: Tue Thu Fri Sun 10:00-17:00, Wed Sat 10:00-20:00
voyage.content: The German Movie Museum displays—as the name implies—the art and history of film making (German only)

voyage.name: Ikonen Museum
voyage.price: €6, concessions €4, every last Saturday in the month free entrance
voyage.content: Founded in 1990 through a donation of 800 icons from the 16th-19th century this museum today has about 1,000 icons and today also has special exhibitions for modern icons.

voyage.name: Sachsenhausen
voyage.content: By crossing one of the bridges from the city centre you reach the Sachsenhausen part of the city south of the Main river.

voyage.name: Eintracht Frankfurt
voyage.content: Die Adler (The Eagles) play football (soccer) in Bundesliga, the top tier. The stadium (sponsored as Deutsche Bank Park) has a capacity of 51,500, and in 2024 it hosted games in the UEFA Euro Finals. The women's team play in their top tier at Stadion am Brentanobad.

voyage.name: Flea Market
voyage.content: Along the river in Sachsenhausen during which time the road is normally closed to traffic.

voyage.name: Hey Jerry - Sandwiches & Co.
voyage.content: Their chicken-tikka with fries sub would do a British take-away proud. Very basic but good value.

voyage.name: Oberschweinstiege
voyage.content: German restaurant and beer garden in the woods south of the city. Good food (German and vegetarian) and drinks. Only negative is very close to airport runways so can be noisy at times.

voyage.name: Zum gemalten Haus
voyage.content: Restaurant serving traditional local dishes, located in a building with painted façades.

voyage.name: Emma Metzler
voyage.hours: Tue-Sat 12:00–23:00, Sun 12:00–18:00, kitchen has limited hours: Tue-Sat 12:00–14:00 and 18:00–22:00, Sun 12:00–15:00
voyage.content: A relaxed international-local cuisine with great service and changing menu. Set in the Bauhaus-Style Museum für Angewandte Kunst (Museum of Applied Arts), close to the Main river, but with no view. Quite recommendable. Suitable for vegetarians.

voyage.name: Taj Mahal
voyage.content: Good Indian restaurant with short walk from city centre. Reservation for dinner is recommended.

voyage.name: Youth Hostel Frankfurt
voyage.content: The official youth hostel of Hostelling International and the German branch. Prices are lower with HI membership but its open for all travellers. Dorms, family and single rooms.

voyage.name: Hotel am Berg
voyage.content: The place is decorated kind of old-style. 20 minutes walk to the centre. It is an old half-timbered style mansion, giving more the feeling of a B&B than a hotel and each room has its own eccentric décor.

voyage.name: Hotel Cult
voyage.content: Excellent 4-Star Desinghotel in Frankfurt/Sachsenhausen.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Hotel Frankfurt Airport North
Sheraton Frankfurt Congress Hotel - Niederrad
voyage.content: Do not mistake this hotel and the other Sheraton at the airport.

voyage.name: Lindner Main Plaza
voyage.content: Stunning views over the skyline of Frankfurt and directly on the river.

voyage.name: Hilton Garden Inn Frankfurt Airport
voyage.content: Directly connected to Terminal 1. The hotel is equipped with soundproofed guest rooms, business zone and event space.

voyage.name: Höchst Old Town
voyage.content: The old town of Höchst with its castle and small medieval streets full of half-timbered houses.

voyage.name: Petrihaus
voyage.content: The picturesque and unique Swiss style pavillon once hosted famous German poets like Goethe and Brentano. Refurbished in 2002, it is open for guided tours. Located in a nice park which has a faded rose garden, some art nouveau sculptures, Europe's oldest gingko-tree and plenty of lawn to enjoy a splendid day.

voyage.name: Verkehrsmuseum Frankfurt am Main
voyage.content: Public transportation vehicles including many old trams, a few buses and one steam locomotive. Beside the museum is a station building that used to belong to the former Frankfurter Waldbahn, a tram line that used to be powered by steam locomotives.

voyage.name: Kobelt-Zoo
voyage.content: A small zoo with monkeys, snakes and other animals. Kids can pet rabbits, horses, donkeys, and goats, or ride ponies.

voyage.name: Sportpark Kelkheim
voyage.content: A sports facility complex that features high rope courses, golf (no membership required), indoor climbing and bouldering, squash, and other activities.

voyage.name: Radsport Frankfurt
voyage.content: Exists since 1983 and mostly sells road race bikes. They are passionate for bike sport.

voyage.name: Fahrradhaus Wagner
voyage.content: The small shop at the outskirts of Frankfurt has a long tradition since 1929 selling bikes. One can see their passion for bikes in how well they keep the records of their sold bikes and repairs. The prices are really fair and the road- or mountain-bike can be repaired or tuned at any wish.

voyage.name: Bizim Döner
voyage.content: A small suburban shop with fantastic kebab.

voyage.name: Lahmer Esel
voyage.content: Expands in summer time over to tables in the garden. It has local authentic food to fair prices and good fresh quality. It is popular as after dinner from the Frankfurt Goethe University faculty. The local "Apfelwein" (Ebbelwoi) is recommended.

voyage.name: Speisekammer
voyage.hours: 17:00- during summer, 18:00- winter, Sun lunch too
voyage.content: This traditional place has an idyllic garden with very old trees. The food is typical and very regional, nevertheless it has many options for vegetarians. The present by the house adds to the stylish environment of a pleasureable dinner.

voyage.name: Alte Schiffsmeldestelle
voyage.content: In summertime a relaxed bar with a view of the Höchst castle and the Main river. Good place to stop by on a bike tour from Frankfurt to Wiesabaden.

voyage.name: Ramada Frankfurt Messe
voyage.content: Slightly older but well-maintained hotel located near the Messe exhibition centre, but far from anything else. Pool and gym. Free shuttle from the airport, but €7 for the return trip.

אנדרטת השואה באולם השוק של פרנקפורט
